digest.component_or_area: test suite / unit tests / subprocess and network sentinels
propositions: Five real-subprocess tests in test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py burn ~1s each waiting for a blanket 1s autouse timeout fixture to expire, creating wall-clock races tied to interpreter startup speed.

Three reap tests assert on child-side setup (pidfile, spawn counter, flushed stdout) that only complete before the injected deadline because 1s happens to exceed interpreter startup, not by explicit ordering.
The test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff test must complete two sequential spawns within the same 1s blanket timeout ceiling, creating latent load flakiness in the opposite direction.
The tight_stall fixture injects a 2s low-speed window though its sibling already proved git honors 1s, causing unnecessary test slowness.
Real-time dependencies must be replaced with explicit readiness gates (marker files, PID polling) rather than tuned with luckier numbers to eliminate races on loaded runners.
